D-094-R017: The contract can now say whether a yard or setback is established before anything is drawn: each geometry.constraint_lines entry (the 23-344(b) 100-ft line, the corner area, the 8-ft street-wall band, the setback line) carries a state and a basis, and its geometry is allowed only in the established branch (oneOf; tested by the valid rear-yard fixture and the invalid fixtures).
D-094-R026: Rear-yard checks and envelope rows carry their inputs (name, value, unit, basis), conditions, text and ZR section ids, and input_facts carry key, value, unit, basis, source title and source date, so a later page can print a worked calculation with its source identifiers and dates instead of a bare listing.
D-094-R044: No geometry is invented to fill a layout: a withheld placement may not carry an outline, a not-known rear-yard check may not carry a number, and an area allocation may not carry zone geometry, a unit count or a core position (invalid fixtures synthetic_withheld_placement_with_outline, synthetic_withheld_check_with_number, synthetic_allocation_zone_geometry; refused by both Python validators and the web checks).
D-094-R058: The contract keeps allowance, placement and the apartment-area allocation as separate blocks with their own labels: placement and area_allocation carry the const label Illustrative, and a way rule refuses fitted=true unless the same building's placement is placed and refuses an allocation whose apartment and other areas do not add to its total (S12 tests in Python and on the web).
D-094-R079: The rear yard gets an explicit applicability check per provision: rear_yard.checks has one entry each for ZR 23-344(a), 23-344(b) and 23-344(c)(3) with state applies, not_applicable or not_known, and a not-known check carries no number; this gives the report a place to show 23-344(b) as an open check (the engine and page come in later tasks).
D-094-R082: The contract can carry the pieces of one worked scenario: an illustrative placement with its outline only when placed, its method, basis, measure and conversion statement, conditions, checks and the constraints not checked (not_checked), plus envelope rows for setback, street wall and side yard.
D-094-R091: area_allocation carries ONE share bounded to the existing assumption (minimum 0.60, maximum 0.75; 0.5999 and 0.7501 refused), with the apartment-area, other-area and total square feet, so the drawing and the calculation use the same stated percentage.
D-094-R092: area_allocation and placement carry the measure as the const residential_floor_area (the estimate's own vocabulary) with a const conversion statement; an allocation without the measure or without the conversion statement is refused (synthetic_allocation_without_measure), so zoning floor area is never taken as the plate area without a stated conversion.
D-094-R094: area_allocation has a fitted flag, and a way rule refuses fitted=true unless the same building's placement is placed (Python validators and web checks, S12), so zones can go inside a footprint only after the footprint is fitted; until then the page shows the proportional bar.
D-094-R096: One contract serves both outputs: the 1.5.0 version is accepted by the server (CONTRACT_VERSIONS_WITH_WAY_LAYER) and the web (SUPPORTED_RESULTS_CONTRACT_VERSIONS), and the web checks mirror the placement and area-allocation rules of the Python validators, so the website and the PDF read the same illustration fields under the same rules.
